procedural_matters: The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
SEN 1 did not come to the hearing, the hearing proceeded in accordance with RRS 63.1(b).
The 'Coach Boat' was not identified by the initiator.
The race committee was represented by Miguel Amaral IRO POR (PRO).
Miguel Amaral informed the international jury that it was the technical committee which had rescued SEN 1.
During the hearing the International Jury clarified in accordance with RRS 63.2(c) that the hearing request was not a protest but a request for redress, and proceeded with it accordingly.
The International Jury called Olive Parker IM IRL (chair technical committee) as a witness to give evidence.
facts: During the time of the incident the wind was around 15 knots with 0.5 m waves.
During race 3, SEN 1 capsized at the end of leg 2, at mark 2.
SEN 1 recovered from the capsize, but then capsized again twice.
This was observed by Olive Parker IM IRL (chair technical committee) who was stationed close to the starboard end of the finishing line.
The competitor of SEN 1 (Ousseynou FALL) waved and Olive Parker initially attempted to get the attention of the race committee and the safety boat(s), but was not successful.
Olive Parker then drove her vessel to SEN 1's position and held his boat.
Ousseynou FALL voluntarily climbed into the technical committee vessel and remained in a crouched position.
SEN 1 (the sail boat) was filled with water and the buoyancy bags were nearly unsecured.
Ousseynou FALL's eyes were rolling, he was not communicating in any language and was clearly distressed.
Olive Parker then decided to take Ousseynou FALL ashore and did that.
Meanwhile, a safety boat arrived and towed SEN 1 (the sail boat) to shore.
SEN 1 did not finish race 3 and was scored DNC.
conclusions: Rescuing the competitor of SEN 1, who had himself sought the assistance, was not an improper action of the technical committee.
SEN 1’s score in race 3 was made significantly worse through his own fault. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(1) are not met.
